h: A city I cannot go back to
x: I was born in Donetsk in 1995. My whole childhood was spent in the Voroshylovskyi district: the courtyards, the streets, the way from home to school. It is my home ground, a place I know from memory rather than from maps. In 2012 I left. In 2014 war came to the city, and the way back was closed. I have not been there since. For me, Donetsk 2011 is the only way to go back: to rebuild the city as it was, from photographs, maps and panoramas, without inventing anything. I start with my own district, but I am building all of Donetsk. This city matters to more people than me. There are thousands like me. Stanislav, creator of the project 14 years since I was last home 1995 Born in Donetsk 1995–20

h: A city out of reach for millions
x: Since 7 April 2014, Donetsk has not been under Ukrainian control. On 30 September 2022, Russia declared it Russian territory. The international community does not recognise the annexation. The war in Donbas displaced millions of people. For many of them, as for me, the way home is closed. The city still exists, but it cannot be reached physically. 985,000 people lived in Donetsk before the war 2009 · Wikipedia: Donetsk 1.6 million people displaced by the war in Donbas March 2016 · UN (OHCHR) 12 years the city has been outside Ukrainian control since 7 April 2014 · Wikipedia: Donetsk Thank you, Davito Daveeni, for this film. It preserved Donetsk in 2012, a big, lively, densely populated city,

Not a game inspired by Donetsk but the city itself: living Donetsk in 2011 with a layer of memory on top. Five pillars decide what the game will be. This project is not a way to pass the time. In essence, it is a missing part of me. I am sure that a great many people still consider this city their own and remember it the way I do. It is a part of them. A part that exists but is physically out of reach. Stanislav The main goal “This is not a city inspired by Donetsk. This is Donetsk.” After 20–30 minutes of play, a person should feel two things at once: “I am in the real Donetsk” and “this is a living open world, not a museum”. Layer 1

A systemic open world: traffic, vehicles, residents' daily routines, an economy, the city's reactions and missions. Combat is not the core of the game. Real geometry comes before level-design convenience. Layer 2

“Memory Echoes”: flashbacks to earlier years at real places on Zarichna Street. The city seen through the eyes of someone who grew up there. Five pillars of the game Live in the real city Walk, take the tram and the marshrutka, buy bread, sit on the bench. The city lives without you Residents have homes, jobs and routines. Yards keep their own rhythm through the time of day and the weather. Freedom with consequences The world notices what you do through witnesses, reputation and the militsiya, and responds in proportion. Memory as discovery Real places unlock memories. Exploring the city is how you find the personal story. Small, human stakes Family, friends, neighbours, work and the distric

Every detail carries an evidence class. If a window is not visible in a panorama, it is not in the model. If a size is estimated by eye, the data says so. That keeps the reconstruction honest as it grows to the scale of a city.
Visible in the October 2011 panorama: material, colour, shape, number of windows. 90 reference objects · 419 facade elements
Building footprints and street centrelines from OpenStreetMap. They anchor the geometry but do not prove what stood there in 2011. 126 footprints · snapshot of 22.09.2026
Heights, window sizes, tree positions. Flagged in the data and replaced as soon as a source turns up. 71 trees · 847 fence posts · 106 roofs

In short Donetsk 2011 is a solo open-world reconstruction of Donetsk exactly as it was in October 2011, built in Unreal Engine 5.8 from OpenStreetMap, terrain data and street panoramas of that month. In full Stanislav was born in Donetsk in 1995 and left in 2012. Since 2014 the way home has been closed. Donetsk 2011 is his way back: a reconstruction of the city as it was in October 2011, the month a Google Street View car drove down Zarichna Street. Every street, house and fence is rebuilt from sources: OpenStreetMap outlines, NASA SRTM terrain and the October 2011 panoramas, used only as visual reference. Every estimate is marked as one. Work starts on Zarichna Street in the Voroshylovskyi
